text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly which arm is affected and describe the specific location of your neck pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if the weakness or numbness is more pronounced in specific fingers, such as the thumb, index, and middle fingers versus the ring and little fingers? Also, do you have any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts or holding utensils?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and bilateral hand weakness alongside your diabetes history raises concern for either severe cervical myelopathy or a peripheral neuropathy like diabetic amyotrophy. I need to rule out structural spinal compression immediately, so REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine.
